summary: Round-2 security fix verification. Ran /app/backend/tests/test_security_round2.py (11 passed, 1 skipped) plus live curl checks against localhost:8001. 10/11 review items PASS. 1 FAIL: agent-trace endpoint still leaks PHI (names + phone) inside payload.prompt_preview / payload.reply_preview string fields because the scrub loop only handles top-level string keys and `payload` is a dict.

critical.issue: SEC-002/SEC-006 scrub is incomplete. server.py L785-788 only calls scrub_persisted_text when m['payload'/'message'/'reason'/'detail'] is a *string*; in practice `payload` is a dict containing `prompt_preview` and `reply_preview` string sub-fields that echo dictionary/form PHI. Live check on session b26146a743ab4362a285a4d2583c0ddb found 8 occurrences of 'James Smith' and 1 phone number 415-555-1234 in agent-trace response.

action_items: Fix agent-trace scrub in /app/backend/server.py session_agent_trace(): recurse into nested dict/list payloads instead of only scrubbing top-level string fields. Either call scrub_persisted_text on the JSON-serialized payload or walk the structure so payload['prompt_preview']/'reply_preview' get redacted to [A]/[D]/[F]/[G]. The scrub_persisted_text helper in phi_core/security.py already supports dicts (line ~176), so pass the entire m through a dict-aware scrubber.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L785-788 agent-trace scrub loop: type-guard on `isinstance(m.get(key), str)` silently skips dict payloads, defeating SEC-006 for the endpoint that is most likely to echo raw LLM prompts.
Consider adding an assertion-level unit test that GET /api/sessions/{sid}/agent-trace returns no PHI substrings anywhere in nested payload dicts (currently only covered indirectly).

rca of the issue: Agent-trace PHI leak (only failing item): In /app/backend/server.py line 786-788 the scrubber runs `for key in ('payload','message','reason','detail'): if isinstance(m.get(key), str): m[key] = _scrub(m[key])`. But when agents log LLM turns, `payload` is stored as a dict like {'prompt_preview': '...raw dictionary text with James Smith and 415-555-1234...', 'reply_preview': '...', ...}. The `isinstance(..., str)` guard therefore never matches, and the sub-strings are returned as-is. Fix: replace the loop body with a dict-aware walk (e.g. `m['payload'] = _scrub_json(m['payload'])`) or call scrub_persisted_text through a recursive helper that iterates nested dicts and lists. The scrub_persisted_text function in phi_core/security.py already handles dict input at ~L176; just remove the isinstance guard for the 'payload' key or use the dict overload. Reproduction: `curl -s http://localhost:8001/api/sessions/b26146a743ab4362a285a4d2583c0ddb/agent-trace | grep -c 'James Smith'` returns >0.
